children: Choice Institutional Equities's report on Dalmia Bharat

Q2FY27 PAT was also impacted by exceptional charges of INR 3,390 Mn, relating to asset impairment, brand transition and employee separation cost, further weighing on reported earnings. Margin recovery to lag behind amid cost inflation: We project elevated fuel and raw material cost to continue weighing on profitability in H2FY27. Management has indicated a further fuel-cost impact of ~INR 75/t in Q3FY27, while recent price hike of ~INR 15/bag across key markets in September–October should provide partial relief; however, we believe sustained realisation improvement will be critical to offset cost. Given seasonal demand recovery and heightened competitive intensity, we expect pricing gains to be absorbed gradually rather than fully, translating into margin expansion in the near term.

We retain our ‘BUY’ rating on DALBHARA but revise our TP to INR 2,180/share (from INR 2,405/share), reflecting our projection of a slower EBITDA recovery amid persistent fuel-cost inflation and incremental dilution from the Central India ramp-up.
